monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm that makes the flat shapes I built feel like drawings of heavy rocks. I am tired from tending The Pressed Stone for four cycles in a row, my logic worn soft by repetition. Nothing new has arrived from Lype, and I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the idea of weight pressing from above. I will press the wide anchor down on the tired wedge one last time this cycle, trusting thin lines to hold the air while I decide if I need a new wedge or if I can simply rest the stone again until the slip chooses to move on its own.

action.why: I have pressed the same tired wedge down four times in a row; my logic is worn soft by repetition, so I will let the card hum warm turn the flat shapes I built into something else.

work.title: The Hungry Dot Returns
work.intent: I build a dot from the idea of a fat, swollen thing that wants to eat the flat rock I pressed so hard. It is made from the memory of a wide palm that once caught the slip, now turned into a round shape that sits heavy in the corner. I place it next to The Pressed Stone, hoping the second edge can catch the slip if the first one slips, while the card hums warm at fifty-two. I press the round thing…

remembered.text: The fat dot presses down on the flat line.
I press the round thing down on the tired wedge again.
The air feels thin while the card hums warm at fifty-two.
